title: Postmortem: rerank endpoint capacity drop from approximate-index rebuilds + throttle-loop interaction
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: On 2026-03-05 we observed a sustained capacity drop and elevated tail latency for the embeddings + rerank endpoint. Root cause combined an aggressive approximate-index (ANN) background rebuild that monopolized CPU+IO on ranking controllers with a misconfigured throttle loop that scaled down worker counts while rebuilds were in progress. This led to increased queuing, KV cache misses, and a ~3x P95 latency regression for rerank queries for 27 minutes. Immediate mitigations restored service; long-term fixes are scheduled.
timeline:
2026-03-05T10:03Z: First alerts: rerank-p95 increased from 280ms to 820ms.
2026-03-05T10:06Z: Alert escalation; on-call (Diego) begins investigations.
2026-03-05T10:09Z: Observed controller CPU and disk IO spike on region-us-west-2-rerank-01; ANN background rebuild jobs started at 09:58Z after a scheduled index window.
2026-03-05T10:12Z: Autoscaler logs show throttle-loop triggered scale-down policy because CPU-based metric dipped (background IO masked real work), lowering worker pool by 30%.
2026-03-05T10:15Z: Queues backfilled; KV cache cold misses increased ~4x leading to higher downstream model inference token counts and increased GPU contention.
2026-03-05T10:20Z: Mitigation 1: paused ANN rebuild via controller API; P95 began to drop but remained elevated.
2026-03-05T10:28Z: Mitigation 2: temporarily disabled CPU-only autoscale decisions and forced minimal worker pool; P95 returned to baseline by 10:30Z.
2026-03-05T10:40Z: Monitoring verified steady state, incident declared resolved at 10:45Z.
2026-03-10T14:00Z: Postmortem complete and actions assigned.
root_cause: Two interacting failures: (1) A scheduled approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) index rebuild ran on rank controllers and consumed significant CPU and disk IO. The rebuild job uses single-tenant controller resources without IO throttling. (2) The autoscaler’s throttle loop decision used an aggregate CPU metric that was misleading during rebuilds (background CPU usage suppressed the scaling signal for request-handling processes because of process-level cgroup aggregation), causing it to downscale worker pods while expensive rebuilds were ongoing. The combination created a resource starvation loop that increased queueing and KV cache churn, amplifying latency for rerank requests.
impact: Customer-facing: Rerank API p95 latency regressed from ~280ms to ~820ms for ~27 minutes affecting both hosted and dedicated customers in us-west-2. Volume: ~12k rerank requests affected. No request loss but degraded quality of experience (timeouts increased from 0.02% to 0.5%). Internal: on-call interruption and follow-up engineering time ~14 engineer-hours.
mitigations_short_term:
- Pause ANN index rebuilds mid-job when request latency exceeds threshold (implemented during incident).
- Disable CPU-aggregated downscale decisions for rerank controllers; force min pool size until safer signals are available.
- Increase KV cache warming budget for controllers to reduce cold-miss penalty while workers resettle.
- Added dashboard widget to correlate ANN rebuild jobs with autoscaler decisions.
mitigations_long_term:
- Rework rebuild jobs to use IO and CPU cgroup limits and run as lower-priority batch jobs with explicit backpressure.
- Update autoscaler to use request-oriented metrics (p99 queued requests, backlog length, QPS per-serving-thread) rather than coarse aggregate CPU for downscaling decisions.
- Introduce rebuild-aware autoscaler exemptions: when rebuild job label present, temporarily pin worker pool.
- Improve KV cache prewarming on scale events; persistent cache shard priming and cross-region warm snapshots.
- Add chaos tests that simulate large ANN rebuilds while exercise autoscaler and KV cache behavior in staging.
action_items: ENG-33655: Add IO/CPU limits and nice-level for ANN rebuild jobs (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 5)
ENG-33656: Implement request-based downscale signal in autoscaler (owner: Omar Li, estimate: 8)
ENG-33657: Build controller-side cache prewarm + shard snapshot (owner: Mei Chen, estimate: 5)
ENG-33658: Create test harness to simulate rebuilds + autoscale interactions (owner: Diego Ramirez, estimate: 3)
ENG-33659: Dashboard correlation tile for rebuilds vs autoscale decisions (owner: Monitoring Team, estimate: 2)
metrics: Baseline p95 rerank latency: 280ms; incident peak p95: 820ms. KV cache miss rate baseline: 4%; incident peak: 17%. Worker pool size: scaled down by 30% from 40 -> 28 during incident. Affected request count: ~12,000 over 27 minutes. No increase in error rate (5xx) attributable to model inference but timeouts (client-side) increased from 0.02% to 0.5% during peak.
lessons_learned:
- Background batch jobs that share controller host resources must be IO/CPU-throttled and clearly labeled so autoscalers and monitoring understand their presence.
- Aggregated CPU metrics can be misleading during mixed workload states; autoscalers should prefer request-centered signals for downscale.
- Cache cold starts combined with transient downscales create cascading effects; invest in proactive warming and pinned minimum capacity for critical endpoints.
- Incident detection: add runbook entries for ANN-rebuild correlated alerts to speed mitigation steps.
